technical_and_design_decisions: For U1, enhance user documentation with quick start guides and improved navigation to help new visitors.
For U2, implement new-channel configuration transaction logic based on existing Gerrit change FAB-687 to ensure consistency.
For U3, develop peer upgrade functionality using lifecycle chaincode to allow upgrades without data loss, incorporating patching capabilities.
For U4, refactor ledger code and tests to use new block structure and remove explicit dependencies on MSP security for cleaner code.
For U5, create visual aids using diagramming tools (e.g., PlantUML) and demonstration scripts to explain Fabric v1.0 architecture.
For U6, maintain up-to-date documentation in Markdown format, version-controlled with the codebase, for v1.0 development.
For U7, add sanity checks in chaincode invocation handlers to restrict calls to only LCCC or normal chaincode.
For U8, develop Node SDK using fabric-client library, following standard Node.js patterns for blockchain interaction.
assumptions: I have full access to the Hyperledger Fabric codebase, including relevant Gerrit changes (e.g., 1795, 2581).
The development environment is pre-configured with necessary tools, dependencies, and testing frameworks.
Effort estimates include time for coding, unit testing, basic integration testing, and code reviews.
No major external dependencies or blockers are anticipated, and all user stories are independent enough to be worked on sequentially or in parallel as needed.
I am familiar with Hyperledger Fabric architecture and can handle technical tasks without additional learning curves.

activities.activity_description: Enhance documentation for new visitors to quickly get started and find needed information, including quick start guides and improved navigation.
Develop or integrate the new-channel configuration transaction logic as per FAB-687, ensuring correct fields and values for private transactions.
Implement functionality to upgrade peers without data loss using lifecycle chaincode, including patching capabilities for security or protocol changes.
Update ledger code and tests to use new block structure, remove old structure dependencies, and eliminate MSP security dependencies from unit tests.
Design visual aids (e.g., diagrams) and demonstration scripts to explain Fabric v1.0 architecture and behavior to collaborators and customers.
Produce up-to-date documentation for v1.0 Fabric during development, directing users to v0.6 for stability and covering v1.0 usage.
Add sanity checks in chaincode invocation logic to ensure only LCCC or normal chaincode can be invoked, preventing unauthorized calls.
Create Node.js SDK for developers to interact with the blockchain, including client libraries and APIs for transaction submission and query.
